blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Effective democratic deliberation is vital for civic engagement and the health of legislative institutions. However, assessing parliamentary discourse quality is traditionally done using expert-scored, theory-based codebooks (CBs), which are rigid, labor-intensive, and prone to biases. While Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a scalable alternative for both schema induction and discourse annotation, ensuring schema quality and mitigating models' inherent bias remains a clear challenge. In this work, we propose a complete protocol for LLM-based codebook generation and evaluation. Starting from the widely accepted discourse quality Index (DQI), we compare top-down (theory-based), bottom-up (data-driven), and hybrid approaches for generating context-adapted schemas. To evaluate these schemas, we define an extrinsic proxy measure, validated by manual annotations, alongside an intrinsic inter-model agreement (IMA) metric, which leverages differing model biases to signal overall reliability. Our experiments on 100 Israeli parliament transcripts reveal that inductive, data-driven schemas achieve higher IMA than top-down methods while maintaining validity, demonstrating their potential for reliable, large-scale analysis of political discourse.
blocks.zh: 有效的民主审议对公民参与和立法机构的健康至关重要。 然而,评估议会讨论的质量传统上是使用专家评分、基于理论的法典进行的,这些法典是僵硬的、劳动密集型的,容易出现偏见。 虽然大语言模型(LLMs)为策略诱导和语句注释提供了可扩展的替代方法,但确保策略质量和缓解模型固有的偏差仍然是一项明确的挑战。 在这项工作中,我们提出了基于LLM的代码集生成和评价的完整协议. 从广泛接受的论语质量指数(DQI)开始,我们比较自上而下(基于理论),自下而上(基于数据),以及产生上下文调整的策略的混合方法. 为了评估这些计划,我们界定了一种外在代用措施,通过人工说明加以验证,同时确定一个内在的模型间协议(IMA)衡量标准,利用不同的模型偏差来显示总体可靠性。 我们对100份以色列议会记录的实验表明,由数据驱动的诱导性计划比自上而下的方法取得了更高的IMA,同时保持了有效性,显示了它们对政治言论进行可靠和大规模分析的潜力。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Deliberation is the interactive process where individuals engage in discussion to reach rational conclusions, occurring in both formal political bodies and local civic settings. At its core lies the premise that political decision-making should be talk-centric rather than vote-centric ( Steenbergen et al., 2003 ) . Effective democratic deliberation is crucial for civic engagement and the health of legislative institutions ( Serrano-Contreras et al., 2020 ; Schroeder et al., 2024 ; Tschentscher et al., 2010 ) . Prominent literature identifies thoughtful analysis, open-mindedness, mutual respect, and participants’ willingness to revise their initial preferences through discourse as prerequisites for this efficacy ( Steenbergen et al., 2003 ; Ercan et al., 2022 ) .
blocks.zh: 思考是个人参与讨论以达成合理结论的互动进程,在正式政治机构和地方公民环境中都发生。 其核心前提是,政治决策应以谈话为中心,而不是以投票为中心(Steenbergen等,2003年)。 有效的民主审议对公民参与和立法机构的健康至关重要(Serrano-Contreras等,2020年;Schroeder等,2024年;Tschentscher等,2010年)。 著名文献指出,通过讨论修改其初步偏好的意愿是这种功效的先决条件(Steenbergen等人,2003年;Ercan等人,2022年)。

blocks.en: Quantifying deliberation quality enables its application to downstream tasks, such as identifying anomalous deliberative behavior, evaluating the performance of legislators, and alerting civic facilitators when participant satisfaction could be improved ( Schroeder et al., 2024 ) . But while numerous factors have been argued to affect discourse quality, such as domination, issue polarization, and agenda setting ( Kumar et al., 2025 ; Serrano-Contreras et al., 2020 ) , quantifying this quality remains challenging due to the inherent competing interests between interlocutors, rhetorical ambiguity, and the variance in acceptable standards across societies and domains.
blocks.zh: 量化审议质量可以使其适用于下游任务,例如确定反常的审议行为、评价立法者的业绩,以及提醒公民促进者,因为参与者的满意度可以提高(Schroeder等,2024)。 但是,尽管有许多因素被认为影响了言论的质量,如统治、问题分化和议程制定(Kumar等人,2025年;Serrano-Contreras等人,2020年),但由于对话者之间固有的竞争利益、言辞模糊以及社会和领域在可接受的标准上的差异,量化这种质量仍然具有挑战性。

blocks.en:
Various methods, including computational frameworks, have been proposed for measuring multi-party discourse quality ( Steenbergen et al., 2003 ; Behrendt et al., 2024 ; Bosley, 2025 ) . A common protocol for quality assessment involves experts evaluating live multi-party discourse using a theoretical-scientific scoring schema. This schema, known as a codebook (CB), comprises categories that reflect rationality, reciprocity, and civility, and uses ordinal scales to individually assess each criterion ( Behrendt et al., 2024 ; Graham, 2010 ; Esau et al., 2021 ; Bächtiger et al., 2010 ; Steenbergen et al., 2003 ) .
However, this paradigm has various limitations. First, rigid, theory-based schemas often struggle to generalize across topic-dependent or culture-dependent nuances. Second, collecting human annotation is labor-intensive and inherently subject to individual biases ( Romberg et al., 2025 ; Vecchi et al., 2025 ; Brown et al., 2025 ) .
blocks.zh:
提出了各种衡量多党言论质量的方法,包括计算框架(Steenbergen等,2003年;Behrendt等,2024年;Bosley,2025年)。 质量评估的共同协议涉及专家利用理论科学评分计划对多党对话进行现场评价。 这一计划被称为一种编码本(CB),包含反映合理性、互惠性和文明性的类别,并使用平面尺度单独评估每项标准(Behrendt等,2024;Graham等,2010;Esau等,2021;Bächtiger等,2010;Steenbergen等,2003)。
然而,这种模式有各种局限性。 首先,僵硬的、以理论为基础的计划往往努力将各种依赖主题或文化的细微差别概括起来。 第二,收集人的注释是劳动密集型的,并必然受到个人偏见的影响(Romberg等,2025;Vecchi等,2025;Brown等,2025)。

blocks.en: To automate the application of such schemas, researchers have employed supervised machine learning Fournier-Tombs and Di Marzo Serugendo (2020) ; Fournier-Tombs and MacKenzie (2021) ; Berkovitz et al. (2023) and Large Language Models (LLMs) ( Bosley, 2025 ; Langlais et al., 2025 ; Chen et al., 2026 ) . However, both approaches still rely upon the same rigid frameworks.
blocks.zh: 为了实现这种计划应用的自动化,研究人员雇用了受监督的机器学习Fournier-Tombs和Di Marzo Serugendo(2020年);Fournier-Tombs和MacKenzie(2021年);Berkovitz等人(2023年)和大语言模型(LLMs)(Bosley,2025年;Langlais等人,2025年;Chen等人,2026年)。 然而,这两种办法仍然依赖同样的僵硬框架。

blocks.en: In this work, we propose Computational Discourse Quality Index (C-DQI), a methodology for the definition and application of CBs for assessing discourse quality. We explore four distinct workflows for C-DQI CB generation. We start with a baseline adapted from Steenbergen et al. (2003) ’s Discourse Quality Index (DQI) and implement three pipelines that deploy LLMs for CB induction, differing in their balance of top-down (theory-based) and bottom-up (data-driven) approaches.
blocks.zh: 在这项工作中,我们提出计算演讲质量指数(C-DQI),这是用于评估演讲质量的CB的定义和应用方法. 我们为C-DQI CB生成探索出四个截然不同的工作流程. 我们首先根据Steenbergen等人(2003年)的《论文质量指数》调整了基线,并实施了三条管线,部署LLMs用于CB入门,这在自上而下(基于理论)和自下而上(基于数据)方法的平衡上有所不同。

blocks.en:
To evaluate the CBs, we propose both intrinsic and extrinsic measures. Following Steenbergen et al. (2003) , who discuss the importance of robustness in a discourse quality index, and acknowledging that LLMs are inherently pre-trained with internal biases ( Mor-Lan et al., 2026 ) , we argue that the consensus of multiple models indicates that the CBs’ criteria are reliable for LLM annotation, rather than artifacts of a single model. We thus propose to define Inter-Model Agreement (IMA) scores across multiple LLMs to capture intrinsic reliability.
A higher IMA score indicates a clearer, more objective, and robust framework for automated protocol annotation. However, because agreement does not equate to validity, we further compare the CBs’ overall assessments against human-validated proxies for deliberation quality, utilizing both manual and automatic annotations. Figure 1 demonstrates the full C-DQI pipeline and evaluation process.
blocks.zh:
为了评估能力建设,我们提出了内在和外在措施。 Steenbergen等人(2003年)讨论了稳健性在讨论质量指数中的重要性,并承认LLMs在本质上受到内部偏见的预先训练(Mor-Lan等人,2026年),我们提出,多种模型的共识表明CB标准对于LLM注释是可靠的,而不是单一模型的文物. 因此,我们提议界定跨多个有限责任公司(LLM)的《模式间协定》分数,以掌握固有的可靠性。
更高的IMA分数表明自动协议注释的更清晰,更客观,更坚固的框架. 但是,由于协议并不等同于有效性,我们进一步比较了能力建设委员会的总体评估与经人验证的评议质量代理人,同时使用人工说明和自动说明。 图1显示了完整的C-DQI管道和评价过程。

blocks.en: To assess the efficacy of our proposed workflows, we apply different LLMs to annotate a corpus of 100 committee meeting transcripts from the Israeli parliament, the Knesset, according to each CB. The data spans multiple governments and a diverse range of bills, providing a dynamic, culture-dependent environment for examining discourse quality. Utilizing this region-specific data demonstrates the cultural alignment challenges inherent in analyzing localized political discourse.
blocks.zh: 为了评估我们拟议工作流程的功效,我们采用不同的法学硕士课程,从以色列议会和以色列议会,根据每个联邦统计局,对100份委员会会议记录进行注释。 这些数据涉及多个政府和各种法案,为审查讨论质量提供了一个动态的、以文化为基础的环境。 利用这一针对具体区域的数据表明,分析地方政治言论本身就存在文化协调方面的挑战。

blocks.en:
Our results reveal that bottom-up CBs exhibit higher IMA, while all CBs correlate comparably with the quality proxy ( ρ \rho > 0.58), demonstrating that data-driven schema generation yields more reliable evaluations without sacrificing validity.
Through this work, our primary contributions are twofold: (1) we develop a computational tool that automatically defines and evaluates discourse quality CBs for multi-party discussions and scores the data accordingly; and (2) we provide empirical insights into the optimal balance between top-down theoretical frameworks and bottom-up, inductive approaches for yielding reliable evaluation criteria.
blocks.zh:
我们的结果表明,自下而上的国家能力建设显示更高的IMA,而所有的国家能力建设都与质量代用物(à\rho > 0.58)相对应,表明数据驱动的生成计划产生更可靠的评价,而不牺牲有效性。
通过这项工作,我们的主要贡献是两方面的:(1)我们开发一个计算工具,为多党讨论自动定义和评价讨论质量的CB,并据此对数据进行评分;(2)我们对自上而下理论框架与自下而上、自上而上产生可靠评价标准的最佳平衡提供经验见解。

blocks.en: 2 Background
blocks.zh: 2 背景情况

blocks.en:
A widely applied measure for deliberative quality is the Discourse Quality Index (DQI) originally developed for the analysis of parliamentary debates ( Steenbergen et al., 2003 ) .
The DQI is theoretically grounded in established discourse ethics and its schema includes criteria representing norms that discourse is expected to satisfy. Its unit of analysis is an individual speech, defined as “the public discourse by a particular individual delivered at a particular point in a debate” (§ 4.2 provides further details).
blocks.zh:
对议事质量的一个广泛应用的衡量标准是最初为分析议会辩论而制订的论文质量指数(Steenbergen等,2003年)。
DQI在理论上以既定的论述道德为基础,其方案包括代表论述可望满足的准则的标准。 其分析单位是个人演讲,被定义为“特定个人在辩论的某一时刻发表的公开言论”(第4.2节提供了进一步的细节)。

blocks.en: Yet, this de facto standard is constrained by drawbacks tied directly to the DQI framework, as well as broader limitations inherent to predefined schemas. First, despite well-defined coding categories, the DQI does not prescribe a standardized procedure for aggregating category-level annotations into a single discourse-level score, complicating its use in large-scale automated evaluation ( Steenbergen et al., 2005 ) . Second, according to the DQI, off-topic discourse and clarifying questions are excluded from the final score, and interruptions are only accounted for if participants complain about them, ignoring the potential for these factors to contribute to the overall quality assessment.
blocks.zh: 然而,这一事实上的标准受到直接与DQI框架有关的缺陷以及预先界定的计划所固有的更广泛限制的限制。 首先,尽管编码类别定义明确,但DQI并没有规定将类别级说明汇总为单一的会话级分数的标准程序,使其在大规模自动化评价中的使用复杂化(Steenbergen等,2005年). 第二,根据"DQI",在最终分数中排除了非主题的论述和澄清问题,只有在参与者抱怨时才计入中断,而忽略了这些因素对整体质量评估的贡献潜力.

blocks.en: More generally, hard-coded CBs target specific settings and contexts, and therefore struggle to generalize to topic-dependent or culture-dependent contexts; and manually annotating them is labor-intensive and inherently subject to individuals’ biases ( Romberg et al., 2025 ; Vecchi et al., 2025 ; Brown et al., 2025 ) .
blocks.zh: 更一般地说,硬编码的CB针对的是具体的环境和背景,因此很难概括到主题依赖或文化依赖的背景;手动注释这些背景是劳动密集型的,必然受到个人偏见的影响(Romberg等,2025;Vecchi等,2025;Brown等,2025)。

blocks.en: Multiple efforts have operationalized discourse quality assessment by applying supervised machine learning to the DQI ( Fournier-Tombs and Di Marzo Serugendo, 2020 ; Fournier-Tombs and MacKenzie, 2021 ; Berkovitz et al., 2023 ) . Furthermore, Kumar et al. (2025) recently combined argumentation graphs with the DQI for more objective assessment. Deep learning approaches like the AQuA framework successfully bridge NLP with deliberation theory to analyze discourse semantics, though they remain resource-intensive due to the overhead of running multiple fine-tuned BERT adapters ( Behrendt et al., 2024 ) .
blocks.zh: 多项努力通过对DQI(Fournier-Tombs和Di Marzo Serugendo,2020年;Fournier-Tombs和MacKenzie,2021年;Berkovitz等,2023年)应用受监督的机器学习,将讨论质量评估付诸实施。 此外,Kumar等人(2025年)最近将论证图与DQI合并,以便进行更客观的评估。 AQuA框架等深层学习方法成功将NLP与审议理论相接来分析语义学,不过由于运行多台微调BERT适配器的超额操作,它们仍然资源密集(Behrendt等,2024年).

blocks.en: Currently, the field is actively moving toward using LLMs as evaluative agents, bypassing the limitations of manual annotation and rigid linguistic features ( Langlais et al., 2025 ; Chen et al., 2026 ; Bosley, 2025 ) . Specifically, Bosley (2025) evaluated the DQI using a few-shot prompting framework, achieving IMA comparable to human standards. Their work laid the foundation for our methodological study on C-DQI schemas.
blocks.zh: 目前,该领域正积极采用LLMS作为评价代理人,绕过人工注释和刚性语言特征的限制(Langlais等,2025;Chen等,2026;Bosley,2025)。 具体来说,博斯利(2025年)利用几发的提示框架评价了DQI,实现了与人的标准相仿的IMA. 他们的工作为我们关于C-DQI计划的方法研究奠定了基础。

blocks.en: To address the limitations of rigid, predefined schemas, researchers have utilized LLMs for automatic schema definition. Earlier work deploys LLMs to construct literature-review tables by prompting the model to generate a schema and then populating the table from the underlying data ( Newman et al., 2024 ) , optionally conditioned on a user-provided intent ( Padmakumar et al., 2025 ) .
blocks.zh: 为了解决僵硬的、预先界定的计划的局限性,研究人员利用LLMs进行自动的计划定义。 早期的工作部署LLMs来构建文献审查表,方法是促使模型生成一个计划,然后从基础数据中填入该表(Newman等人,2024年),可选择以用户提供的意图为条件(Padmakumar等人,2025年)。

blocks.en: More recently, human-in-the-loop systems have been developed to automate schema definition over large corpora of unstructured text, including ScheMatiQ ( Levy et al., 2026 ) and Schema-miner pro ( Sadruddin et al., 2025 ; Sadruddin et al., 2026 ) . These systems combine prompting pipelines with interactive interfaces and agentic tooling.
blocks.zh: 最近,开发了人-在-在-在-在-在(Sadruddin等,2025;Sadruddin等,2026)。 这些系统将导管与交互式接口和代理工具相结合。

blocks.en: To our knowledge, however, the outputs of these systems have been evaluated mainly for their agreement with expert-annotated schemas, rather than being systematically assessed for intrinsic reliability, which we emphasize in our current work.
blocks.zh: 然而,据我们所知,对这些系统的产出进行了评价,主要是因为它们同意专家说明的计划,而不是为了我们在当前的工作中强调的内在可靠性而进行系统评估。

blocks.en: 3 The Challenge
blocks.zh: 3个 挑战

blocks.en: Without systematically evaluating codebook efficacy, the question remains: How can we derive new or adapted schemas for new settings and domains? How can we determine whether a schema is good ? And, how can we avoid the undermining effects of inherent biases of individual LLMs?
blocks.zh: 在不系统地评价代码手册效力的情况下,问题仍然是: 我们如何为新的环境和领域制定新的或经过调整的计划? 我们如何确定一个计划是否良好? 而且,我们如何避免个别法学硕士的固有偏见所造成的损害?

blocks.en: 4 A Complete Protocol for LLM-based Codebook Generation and Evaluation
blocks.zh: 4 以LLM为基础的守则编制和评价的完整协议

blocks.en:
To remove the reliance on rigid CBs that require manual annotation,
we propose an LLM-based methodology for effective and efficient definition and application of a Computational Discourse Quality Index (C-DQI). This methodology addresses the core limitations of traditional schema-based annotations by allowing for flexible schema induction across different contexts and replacing human annotators with LLMs to mitigate subjective human biases.
blocks.zh:
消除对需要人工注释的僵硬CB的依赖,
我们提出了一个基于LLM的方法,以便有效和高效地界定和应用计算论文质量指数。 这种方法解决了基于传统计划的说明的核心局限性,允许在不同情况下灵活地进行计划诱导,并用LLMs取代人的注释器来减轻主观的人类偏见.

blocks.en: In § 4.1 we introduce C-DQI, used to quantify quality based on a codebook. In § 4.2 we then define the computation task of codebook induction and its various variants, and finally in § 4.3 we define metrics that aim to assess the reliability and validity of the generated codebook.
blocks.zh: 在§ 4.1中,我们引入了C-DQI,用来根据代码表量化质量. 在§4.2中,我们随后界定了代码取用及其各种变体的计算任务,最后在§4.3中,我们界定了旨在评估生成的代码的可靠性和有效性的衡量标准。

blocks.en: 4.1 Computational Discourse Quality Index
blocks.zh: 4.1 计算论文质量指数

blocks.en:

Let D D be an input transcript and C C be a given CB. The input transcript D D is split into multiple segments D = ( s 1 , s 2 , … , s n ) D=(s_{1},s_{2},\dots,s_{n}) , and the CB C C defines a set of evaluation categories C = { c 1 , c 2 , … , c m } C=\{c_{1},c_{2},\dots,c_{m}\} where each category is scored on a predefined scale. 1 1 1 We use a 4-point scale. Because DQI assigns each category its own scale, we min-max normalize its raw scores to this range: y ~ = 1 + 3 ​ y − y min y max − y min \tilde{y}=1+3\frac{y-y_{\min}}{y_{\max}-y_{\min}} , where y min , y max y_{\min},y_{\max} are the category’s minimum and maximum possible scores. This keeps all CBs comparable. For every segment-category pair ( s i , c j ) (s_{i},c_{j}) , an LLM annotator M M evaluates the text on the required scale, yielding a score y i , j y_{i,j} . The per-category discussion score, S ⁡ ( c j ) S(c_{j}) , is calculated as the average across all segments: S ⁡ ( c j ) = 1 n ​ ∑ i = 1 n y i , j S(c_{j})=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}y_{i,j} This final index, representing the overall discourse quality for the transcript, is the average over all categories: C-DQI ​ ( D , M ) = 1 m ​ ∑ j = 1 m S ⁡ ( c j ) \text{C-DQI}(D,M)=\frac{1}{m}\sum_{j=1}^{m}S(c_{j}) When a single comprehensive score per transcript is required, we report the mean of the C-DQI scores produced by the ensemble of annotator models.

blocks.en: 4.2 LLM-based Codebook Generation
blocks.zh: 4.2 基于 LLM 的代码集生成

blocks.en: We define the task of CB generation as a function from texts to a set of categories. Formally, let T T be a collection of texts and let C = { c 1 , … , c n } C=\{c_{1},\dots,c_{n}\} be a finite set of categories describing dimensions for evaluating discourse; the CB generation task is defined as f ⁡ ( T ) = C f(T)=C .
blocks.zh: 我们把CB生成的任务定义为从文本到一组类别的函数. 形式上,让T成为文本的集合,让C={c 1,.,cn} C=\{c_{1},\dots,c_{n}\}}成为一组限定的类别,描述评价讨论的维度;CB生成任务被定义为f  (T) = C f(T)=C.

blocks.en:
Specifically, we implement four workflows to derive CBs.
One is a standard baseline, and three are LLM-based — one receives academic literature as the input text ( top-down ), the second reviews transcripts from the domain being studied ( bottom-up ), and the third combines both inputs ( hybrid ) (see Figure 1 ). All prompts are available in Appendix A .
blocks.zh:
具体地说,我们执行四个工作流程来得出CB.
一是标准基线,三是基于LLM的——一是接收作为输入文本的学术文献(自上而下),二是来自被研究域的评议笔录(自下而上),三是兼收并蓄两种输入(混合) (见图一). 所有提示都载于附录A。

blocks.en: The baseline workflow adapts the original Discourse Quality Index (DQI), which features seven coding categories: (1) participation, (2) level of justification, (3) content of justification, (4) respect for the groups to be helped by particular policies, (5) respect toward the demands of others, (6) respect toward counterarguments, and (7) constructive politics.
blocks.zh: 基线工作流程调整了最初的论文质量指数(DQI),该指数有7个编码类别:(1) 参与,(2) 说明理由的程度,(3) 说明理由的内容,(4) 尊重受特定政策帮助的群体,(5) 尊重他人的要求,(6) 尊重反证,和(7) 建设性政治。

blocks.en: Deriving the final score involves coding all speeches and interpreting their criteria scores. The authors define relevant speeches as ones containing a policy proposal (originally termed a ‘demand’).
blocks.zh: 最终分数的产生涉及对所有发言进行编码并解释其标准分数. 作者将相关发言定义为包含政策建议(原称 " 需求 " )的发言。

blocks.en: The coding process requires initial filtering to distinguish relevant excerpts, which are then scored per category. For this workflow, we adapt the authors’ original coding guidelines ( Steenbergen et al., 2005 ) by assigning numerical values to their scales and adjust the unit of analysis from individual speeches to segments of up to 1,500 words to maintain consistency with our other CBs.
blocks.zh: 编码过程需要初始过滤以区分相关节录,然后按类别分出. 对于这一工作流程,我们调整了作者最初的编码准则(Steenbergen等,2005年),将数字值分配到他们的尺度,并将分析单位从单个演讲调整到最多1,500个字的片段,以保持与我们其他CB的一致性。

blocks.en: To define the theory-driven ( Top-Down ) CB, we provide an LLM with a selection of academic literature on deliberation to generate a set of categories. We begin by prompting the literature-survey tool developed by Gupta (2026) with the instruction: “List 10 foundational academic papers on democratic deliberation, in order to develop a discourse quality index”, followed by an iterative process of refining the results according to our prior knowledge and available sources.
blocks.zh: 为了定义由理论驱动(Top-Down)的CB,我们提供了一个LLM,其中选取了一些关于考虑的学术文献来生成一组类别. 我们首先提出了由Gupta(2026年)开发的文献调查工具,其指示是:“列出关于民主审议问题的10个基础学术文件,以制定讨论质量指数”,然后根据我们以往的知识和现有资料来源,进行反复的改进结果的进程。

blocks.en: The resulting list ranges from sources studying Habermas’s discourse ethics ( Heath, 2019 ) to methodological articles ( Steenbergen et al., 2003 ; Stromer-Galley, 2007 ) . The selection also includes frameworks for evaluating deliberative quality ( Mansbridge et al., 2012 ) and sources providing dimensions for evaluation rooted in deliberative theory ( Friess and Eilders, 2015 ) .
blocks.zh: 由此产生的列表从研究哈伯马斯的言论伦理学的来源(Heath,2019)到方法论文章(Steenbergen等,2003;Stromer-Galley,2007.). 选择还包括评价议事质量的框架(Mansbridge等,2012年)和提供基于议事理论的评价内容的来源(Friess和Eilders,2015年)。

blocks.en: We then instruct Gemini-3.1-Pro 2 2 2 https://gemini.google.com/ to define metrics for evaluating the quality of discourse in the selected dataset, based on the frameworks from the selected sources. The response serves as the Top-Down CB.
blocks.zh: 然后,我们指示双子座-3.1-Pro 2 2 https://gemini.google.com/根据选定来源的框架,确定评价选定数据集中讨论质量的尺度。 反应是顶下CB。

blocks.en: To define the inductive ( Bottom-Up ) CB, we prompt Gemini-3.1-Pro with 10 random transcripts to generate evaluation metrics from empirical data. To prevent contamination, these transcripts are excluded from later experiments. Ultimately, this workflow yields three CB variants: Bottom-Up-English , generated from an English prompt; Bottom-Up-Hebrew , generated from a Hebrew prompt; and Bottom-Up-Corrected , which we, as native Hebrew speakers, merged from the two, edited for content, and standardized in structure ( Appendix D ).
blocks.zh: 为了定义诱导性(自下而上)CB,我们用10个随机笔录来提示双子座-3.1-Pro从经验数据中生成评价度量. 为防止被污染,这些记录稿被排除在以后的试验之外。 最终,这一工作流程产生了三种CB变体:由英文提示生成的Bottom-Up-English;由希伯来语提示生成的Bottom-Up-Hebrew;和由Bottom-Up-Corrected ,我们作为讲希伯来语的本地人,将两者合并,按内容编辑,结构标准化(附录D)。

blocks.en: The Hybrid C-DQI CB combines both the theory-led and inductive approaches. We generate this CB by instructing Google’s Gemini Notebook 3 3 3 https://notebooklm.google.com to synthesize the previously selected academic sources with the empirical transcripts, to create a unified set of metrics for evaluating discourse quality in general committee meetings.

blocks.en: 4.3 LLM-based Codebook Evaluation
blocks.zh: 4.3 以LLM为基础的守则评价

blocks.en: We define the measure of reliability as the consistency of the generated CBs, calculated based on IMA scores and averaged over each CB’s criteria.
blocks.zh: 我们把可靠性的衡量标准定义为根据IMA的分数计算得出并平均衡量每个CB的标准所产生的CB的一致性.

blocks.en: Steenbergen et al. (2003) name four properties that a measure of discourse quality must exhibit: theoretical grounding , reliance on observable phenomena , generalizability , and reliability . To evaluate reliability , they use the ratio of agreement among coders, Cohen’s κ \kappa , Spearman’s ρ \rho , and the standardized α \alpha .
blocks.zh: Steenbergen等人(2003年)列举了衡量言论质量必须表现出的四种特性:理论基础、依赖可观测现象、普遍性和可靠性。 为了评价可靠性,他们使用编码者、科恩的"\kappa"、斯皮尔曼的"\rho"和标准化的"α"之间的协议比例。

blocks.en: Inter-annotator agreement serves as a lens into the complexity of the task and the quality of the annotations. Higher values indicate that the definitions are clear for different coders, whereas lower values suggest both annotator performance issues and poorly defined categories.
blocks.zh: 说明人之间的协议有助于透视任务的复杂性和说明的质量。 较高的数值表明,不同编码者的定义是明确的,而较低的数值则表明说明器的性能问题和定义不清的类别。

blocks.en: We introduce Inter-Model Agreement (IMA) to quantify consensus across different models. Because these LLMs are developed by diverse organizations on distinct training data ( Shmidman et al., 2026 ; Anthropic, 2026 ; Gemma Team, 2026 ; Jiang et al., 2023 ; Bai et al., 2023 ) , we hypothesize they exhibit divergent inherent biases; prior research on cultural biases validates this premise ( Mor-Lan et al., 2026 ) . This diversity contrasts with human annotators, who often share demographic backgrounds or subjective opinions. Consequently, high IMA serves as a compelling measure of robustness. If multiple models agree on the scoring criteria, it indicates that the CBs are reliable for LLM annotation, rather than reflecting the artifacts of a singular model. Thus, a higher agreement score indicates a clearer, more objective, and robust framework for automated protocol annotation.
blocks.zh: 我们采用《模式间协定》,以量化不同模式的共识。 由于这些有限责任公司是由不同的组织根据不同的培训数据(Shmidman等,2026年;Anthropic等,2026年;Gemma Team等,2026年;Jiang等,2023年;Bai等,2023年)开发的,我们假设它们表现出不同的固有偏见;以前对文化偏见的研究证实了这一前提(Mor-Lan等,2026年)。 这种多样性与人类的注释者形成了鲜明的对比,他们往往有着共同的人口背景或主观观点. 因此,高度的IMA是强健的有力尺度。 如果多个模型就打分标准达成一致,则表明CB对LLM注释是可靠的,而不是反映单数模型的文物. 因此,协议得分较高表明,协议自动说明的框架更加明确、更加客观和有力。

blocks.en: Following standard practices for evaluating the DQI, we report the percent agreement as a baseline measure of consensus. To rigorously account for chance agreement, we include Krippendorff’s α \alpha ( Krippendorff, 2011 ) ; values range from -1 to 1; negative values indicate systematic disagreement, while values above zero indicate a degree of agreement. Furthermore, we use Spearman’s ρ \rho to capture annotator agreement on the relative ranking of discussion quality, and the Standardized α \alpha to evaluate the overall internal consistency of the aggregated index.
blocks.zh: 遵循评估DQI的标准做法,我们报告百分率协议作为共识的基准度量. 为了严格说明机会协议,我们列入了克里彭多夫的α-α (Krippendorff, 2011) ; 数值从 - 1 到 1; 负值表示系统性的分歧,而高于零值表示某种程度的一致. 此外,我们利用Spearman的\rho来获取关于讨论质量相对排名的注释员协议,以及标准化的α\alpha来评价汇总指数的整体内部一致性。

blocks.en:
To validate the CBs’ overall performance, we compare their final scores against proxies for discourse quality. For each discussion transcript, we calculate this proxy score by prompting an independent LLM to holistically assess sequences of turns, using a short-context sliding window. These LLM assessments are validated by human annotators to ensure they adequately capture conversational dynamics. This procedure serves as an extrinsic measure of how accurately each schema captures overall discourse quality.
We define this automated proxy for every transcript, represented as a sequence of turns D = ( t 1 , … , t k ) D=(t_{1},\dots,t_{k}) . The task scores the conversation dynamics of an n n -turn exchange on a binary scale, where 0 0 reflects negative deliberation and 1 1 indicates positive deliberation (see Appendix B for the detailed instructions). We use a sliding window of size n = 3 n=3 and score each window independently. The final proxy score for a conversation is the average of all its triplet scores ( p i p_{i} ):

blocks.en: 6 Experimental Setup
blocks.zh: 6 实验设置

blocks.en:
We aim to empirically assess the proposed LLM-based CB generation pipeline using our proposed metrics.
We evaluate each of the four CB generation strategies, comparing the top-down, bottom-up, and hybrid scenarios.
blocks.zh:
我们的目标是利用我们提议的衡量标准,实证地评估拟议的基于LLM的CB发电管道。
我们评估四个CB生成策略中的每一个,比较自上而下,自下而上,和混合的情景.

blocks.en:
Drawing on the 100 transcript selection (§ 5 ),
we segment the discussion into smaller units of analysis, defined as text excerpts of up to 1,500 words and ensuring that individual turns are not split. This text length provides sufficient context for analyzing interaction dynamics and responsiveness, as the median turn length is 10 words. This results in a total of 700 segments for the full corpus, with the majority exceeding 1,466 words ( Table 1 ).
blocks.zh:
根据100份笔录选择(第5节),
我们把讨论分成较小的分析单元,即最多1 500个字的文字节选,并确保不将个别转折分开。 这一文本长度为分析互动动态和响应性提供了足够的上下文,因为中位转长为10个字. 这导致总共700个部分的完整体,大多数超过1 466个字(表1)。

blocks.en: For the open-weight models, we use default hyperparameters with temperature 0.6. We run each model using two seeds (11, 22) and report the mean. For Claude, due to cost considerations, we perform a single run with the temperature 1.0.

blocks.en: We prompt each model with every category-segment pair. Apart from the Vanilla C-DQI CB, which utilizes category-specific scales, all categories are scored on a four-point scale. To create a final, representative vector of deliberation criteria for an entire discussion, the segment-level scores for each category are averaged. The final C-DQI score for a given discussion is determined according to the definitions in § 4.1 .
blocks.zh: 我们每个模型 与每个类别对。 除了使用特定类别分级表的"香草C-DQI CB"外,所有类别均以四分制分级. 为了为整个讨论建立一个最终的、有代表性的审议标准载体,每个类别的分级分数是平均的。 特定讨论的最后C-DQI分数根据§ 4.1中的定义确定.

blocks.en: With a team of domain experts, we manually annotated 162 exchanges to serve as a human benchmark, attaining a Krippendorff’s α \alpha of 0.79 for inter-annotator agreement in a complete overlap setting where each exchange was reviewed by exactly two annotators. Exchanges on which the annotators disagreed were discarded.
blocks.zh: 由域名专家组成的团队,我们手动注释了162次交流,作为人类的基准,在完全重叠的环境下,每一次交流都由两名注释员审查,从而达成Krippendorff的α-α-α为0.79。 注释者不同意的交易所被放弃。

blocks.en: We then deployed GPT-6-luna 11 11 11 run through the OpenRouter API on October 12, 2026: https://openrouter.ai/openai/gpt-6-luna-20260922 — an independent LLM not utilized in the CBs’ reliability evaluation — to compute proxy scores across the dataset. Against the human benchmark, this LLM achieved an accuracy of 82% and a macro F1 score of 77% on a held-out test set of 50 samples (see Appendix F ). Deploying an LLM as a judge not only allows us to scale the validation across the entire dataset (a total of 36,341 3-turn exchanges), avoiding costly time and resource constraints, but it also provides a consistent scoring mechanism that mitigates the noise and subjectivity inherent in human annotations. Consequently, we rely on these automated proxy values to validate our experiments. The distribution of the proxy scores across the corpus is provided in Appendix G .
blocks.zh: 2026年10月12日,我们部署GPT-6-luna 11 11通过OpenRouter API运行:https://openrouter.ai/openai/gpt-6-luna-20260922 ——独立LLM在CB的可靠性评价中没有使用——用于计算整个数据集的代理分数. 对照人类基准,这一LLM在50个样本的停放测试中达到82%的精度和77%的宏F1分数(见附录F)。 部署LLM作为法官,不仅使我们能够在整个数据集(共计36 341个3个转弯交换台)中进行验证,避免花费昂贵的时间和资源限制,而且还提供了一个连贯的打分机制来减轻人类说明中固有的噪音和主观性. 因此,我们依靠这些自动代用值来验证我们的实验. 附录G规定了代理分数在各书目中的分布情况。

blocks.en: To assess the generated CBs, we employ the metrics defined in § 4.3 . For CB reliability, we compute IMA scores for each category. 12 12 12 Since the DQI CB includes filtering “relevant speeches” (§ 4.2 ), for the Vanilla DQI we also compute the IMA score for this phase. For validity, we calculate Spearman correlation coefficients between the mean C-DQI scores and the proxy scores.
blocks.zh: 为了评估产生的能力建设,我们采用了第4.3节所定义的衡量标准。 就CB可靠性而言,我们计算每个类别的IMA分数。 12 12 由于DQI CB包括过滤“相关演讲”(第4.2节),我们还计算这一阶段的IMA分数。 对于有效性,我们计算出斯皮尔曼在平均C-DQI分数和代理分数之间的相关系数.

blocks.en: 7.2 CB Validity
blocks.zh: 7.2 CB有效性

blocks.en: In Table 3 , we present the Spearman correlations between the discussion-level CB scores and the C-DQI proxy scores across the 100 transcripts. All correlations exceed 0.55 and are statistically significant ( p < 10 − 9 p<10^{-9} ). Notably, the top-down CB aligns closest to the proxy ( ρ = 0.66 \rho=0.66 ). This suggests that although the proxy annotators received only minimal binary guidelines, the concept of deliberative quality they apply is itself rooted in the literature, which may favor theory-led CB in the resulting rankings.
blocks.zh: 在表3中,我们介绍Spearman在讨论级别CB分数和C-DQI代理分数之间的关联,跨越了100个笔录. 所有关联性都超过0.55并具有统计意义(p < 10-9 p < 10-X-9})。 值得注意的是,自上而下CB最接近代用词(ρ = 0.66\rho= 0.66). 这表明,虽然代理注释员只收到最低限度的二进制准则,但他们所应用的议事质量概念本身就植根于文献中,这可能会有利于理论引导的CB在由此产生的排名中.

blocks.en: 7.3 CB Analysis
blocks.zh: 7.3 化学分析

blocks.en: We examine the criteria of each CB to identify their similarities and divergences.
blocks.zh: 我们审查每个能力建设机构的标准,以确定它们的相似之处和差异。

blocks.en: The only category shared across all CBs is Respect , which appears as three separate dimensions in the original DQI alone. According to the DQI, respect divides into respect toward groups in society, respect toward others, and respect toward contradicting arguments. A dominant category in the theory-led CBs is Constructive Politics , defined as the ability to bridge disagreements and reach practical solutions, consensus, or compromise. The most similar pair of CBs is the Hybrid and Top-Down , sharing five out of six metrics.
blocks.zh: 在所有CB中唯一共享的类别是"尊重"(Reference),这在最初的"DQI"中单独作为三个独立的维度出现. 根据DQI,尊重分为对社会各群体的尊重、对他人的尊重以及对相互矛盾的论点的尊重。 在以理论为主导的能力建设中,一个占主导地位的类别是建设性政治,即弥合分歧并达成实际解决办法、共识或妥协的能力。 最相似的一对CB是"混合"和"上下"(Top-Down),共享了6个公尺中的5个.

blocks.en: Notably, specific categories exist exclusively in the deductive workflows, such as participation, level and content of justification, and reciprocity. Conversely, categories appearing solely in the inductive workflows include procedural decorum, emotional regulation, and moderator efficiency. 13 13 13 For this analysis, the Hybrid workflow is counted as both an inductive and deductive approach.
blocks.zh: 值得注意的是,在减值工作流程中只存在具体类别,如参与、理由的层次和内容以及互惠。 相反,纯出现在入门工作流程中的类别包括程序装饰、情绪调节和主持人效率。 13 13 对于本分析,混合工作流程既被算作入门方法,又被算作入门方法。

blocks.en: 7.4 Discussion
blocks.zh: 7.4 讨论情况

blocks.en: As shown, the data-driven CBs are more stable across LLM annotation than the theory-based CBs. Specific criteria that appear in the inductive CBs such as emotional regulation and moderator efficiency are likely a product of local cultural nuances in the input data of the CB generation phase.
blocks.zh: 如所显示,数据驱动的CB在LLM注释中比以理论为基础的CB更稳定. 诱导性CB中出现的具体标准,如情绪调节和主持人效率,可能是CB生成阶段输入数据中当地文化细微差别的产物.

blocks.en:
To observe how participation dynamics manifest, we re-examine the transcripts from § 5 using the inductive CBs. 14 14 14 on a 1-4 scale The most intensive meeting is scored 2.5 (Bottom-Up-English) and 2.8 (Bottom-Up-Corrected), while the most chair-centered meeting is scored 2.6 and 2.8, respectively. In contrast, the most evenly distributed meetings attain the same scores, 3.0 and 3.2 for the respective CBs.
This suggests these CBs favor balanced participation over heavy dominance, inviting further investigation to systematically explore the interplay between structural meeting dynamics and automated discourse quality assessments.
blocks.zh:
为了观察参与动态的表现,我们利用导引式CB来重新审查第5节的记录。 最密集相会得分为2.5分(Bottom-Up-English)和2.8分(Bottom-Up-Corrected),而最以会椅为中心的相会得分分别为2.6分和2.8分. 相比之下,分配最均匀的会议得分相同,各自的能力建设会议3.0和3.2。
这表明这些能力建设机构赞成平衡参与,而不是重支配地位,因此,请进行进一步调查,系统地探讨结构会议动态和自动讨论质量评估之间的相互作用。

blocks.en: Future directions include applying the C-DQI to analyze fluctuations in deliberative quality across the parliamentary cycle, investigating whether sessions held immediately before recesses exhibit different scores than mid-session meetings and how it systematically varies across the legislative term.
blocks.zh: 未来的方向包括:运用《公民与残疾调查》来分析整个议会周期审议质量的起伏;调查休会前举行的届会是否与会中会议相比分数不同;以及整个立法期间如何系统变化。

blocks.en: Additionally, the C-DQI enables the comparison of discourse quality analysis across different deliberative environments, such as other parliaments, alternative Israeli legislative bodies, and varying types of Knesset committee protocols.
blocks.zh: 此外,C-DQI使得能够比较不同审议环境,如其他议会、以色列其他立法机构和以色列议会各种类型的委员会议定书的言论质量分析。

blocks.en: The results validate the promise of LLM-driven bottom-up strategies for defining and applying discourse quality schemas. Serving as a proof of concept, our study motivates scaling the generation and annotation of CBs. By maneuvering LLM biases to serve as a feature that enhances robustness, rather than viewing them as unwanted artifacts, future research can uncover new analytical schemes that advance concrete legislative goals.
blocks.zh: 其结果证实了LLM驱动的自下而上的战略对界定和应用讨论质量计划的承诺。 作为概念的证明,我们的研究激励了能力建设的产生和说明。 通过利用LLM偏好作为加强稳健性的特征,而不是把它们看成不需要的文物,未来的研究可以发现新的分析计划来推进具体的立法目标。

blocks.en: 8 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 8 结论

blocks.en: In this study, we proposed a scalable, LLM-driven methodology for generating and validating discourse quality codebooks. Specifically, we examined four approaches for schema definition, deploying an ensemble of diverse LLMs as zero-shot annotators to evaluate the resulting categories. Our results underscore the value of a bottom-up strategy for constructing reliable discourse evaluation frameworks, with validity comparable to theory-based alternatives. Taken together, this work highlights promising avenues for applying our proposed workflow rather than predefined schemas to diverse practical, political, and social scientific investigations.
blocks.zh: 在这项研究中,我们提出了一种可扩展的、LLM驱动的方法,用于生成和验证论述质量的代码本。 具体地说,我们审查了四种计划定义方法,将各种LLMs作为零镜头的注释器,用于评价由此产生的类别。 我们的成果突出表明,自下而上的战略对于建立可靠的言论评价框架具有价值,其有效性可与基于理论的替代办法相媲美。 总之,这项工作突出了将我们拟议工作流程而不是预先确定的计划应用于各种实际、政治和社会科学调查的有希望的途径。

blocks.en: 9 Limitations
blocks.zh: 9 限制

blocks.en: We acknowledge the limitations in our study. Although we rely on LLM-inherent biases in our methodology design, we have not examined how these artifacts manifest in annotating the CBs in practice. Additionally, regarding our choice to use segments of 1,500-words: this aims to capture reciprocity across multiple turns, yet larger segments risk reducing interpretability and introducing noise into holistic scoring. This highlights an inherent tension: higher-level abstractions capture broader dynamics but are harder to evaluate against specific criteria. Despite this, holistic evaluation remains valuable for assessing overarching processes and solutions. In future work, we will explore this in more depth.
blocks.zh: 我们认识到我们研究的局限性。 尽管我们的方法设计中依赖LLM的固有偏见,但我们没有审查这些文物在实践中如何表现在对CB的注释上. 此外,关于我们选择使用1 500个字的片段:其目的是在多个回合之间抓住互惠,但较大的片段有可能降低可解释性,并将噪音引入整体评分。 这凸显出一种内在的紧张:更高层次的抽象反映更广泛的动态,但较难根据具体标准进行评估。 尽管如此,整体评价仍然对评估总体进程和解决办法很有价值。 在今后的工作中,我们将更深入地探讨这一问题。

blocks.en: Regarding the Top-Down CB, the instruction ‘to develop a discourse quality index’ may have biased the model toward the DQI and Habermasian discourse ethics. Further experiments could explore alternative phrasing for the prompt.
blocks.zh: 关于顶级课程, " 制定讨论质量指数 " 的指示可能使模式偏向DQI和Habermasian讨论道德。 进一步的实验可以探索迅速的替代措辞。

blocks.en:
Furthermore, the CBs are evaluated separately as a proof of concept; we did not examine their combinations and other balances besides the hybrid.
Finally, for validity, we rely on statistical correlations. Although a positive correlation indicates the direction of agreement, it doesn’t directly translate to accuracy. We acknowledge this as a limitation. Future research may address this by validating the distributional similarity between CB scores and the proxy C-DQI, and can benefit from a manual gold standard as well.
blocks.zh:
此外,还分别评估能力建设作为概念的证明;我们没有审查混合方案之外的组合和其他平衡。
最后,为了正确起见,我们依靠统计相关性。 虽然正相关关系表明协议的方向, 我们承认这是一种限制。 未来的研究可以通过验证CB分数和代理C-DQI的分布相似性来解决这个问题,并且也可以从手工金本位标准中受益.

must be binary, where 0 reflects poor or destructive deliberation, and 1 indicates
substantive deliberation. • Good interactions (code 1): Statements in which a speaker presents
an opinion or policy demand backed by logical reasoning, evidence, or
justification, while maintaining strict decorum, demonstrating a respectful,
constructive, or appreciative orientation toward other participants and their
counterarguments. • Neutral or poor interactions (code 0): Statements that express
unreasoned claims or non-topical small talk (“neutral”), as well as statements
containing personal attacks, sarcastic degradation, or explicit disrespect toward
other speakers and their demands (“poor”).

blocks.en: Clarifications
blocks.zh: 说明

blocks.en:
• A score of 1 requires both elements: (1) respectful discourse, and
(2) arguments based on internal logic or data. • The definition of 0 includes: procedural statements, cynicism, outbursts,
or a lack of reasoning, neutral stances and concluding remarks. • Asking or answering a question does not qualify as substantive deliberation
unless it directly addresses a contested policy issue with reasons or justification. • Do not judge the validity of the claim, only the manner of its presentation;
we lack the tools to evaluate domain-specific expertise, unless it involves a
blatant falsehood. • Do not consider the role or identity of the speaker when coding. • Judge the interaction as a whole; even if there is a dominant speaker or
turn, that role is given weight, but the other speakers are also considered. • Do not infer deliberative quality from surrounding turns. If the exchange
contains both substantive deliberation and subsequent procedural remarks, score 1
only when the substantive reasoning is an actual part of the exchange and not
merely incidental to an otherwise procedural interaction. • Interruptions (marked as “ - - - ”) are an indication of a
disrespectful discussion, but a single interruption is not decisive on its own. • Fragmented exchanges: count a turn as fragmentary if it is cut off
(“ - - - ”) or is a short interjection of a few words. If two of the
three turns are fragmentary, the speakers are not letting each other finish;
score 0 even if the remaining turn contains a reasoned point. • Implicit cynicism: even if the question is legitimate, the cynical manner
in which it is presented steers the decision toward 0. • Watch for mocking or sarcastic language, such as belittling a
professional’s request for time by mockingly referring to a basic calculation as
a “complex mathematical exercise”, which is considered disrespectful. • Implicit cynicism via rhetorical questioning: If a speaker undermines a
proposal, explanation, or request for authority by using a rhetorical,
challenging question (e.g., mockingly asking “Until now you didn’t need
this?”), it is considered cynical and disrespectful. Score the exchange as 0,
even if the challenged speaker responds in a substantive and professional manner. • Use the provided surrounding context to identify cynicism in the exchange
to rate. • If a participant asks for a date, deadline, or concrete commitment, or
objects that a timeline is too long, a general explanation of the process or a
vague promise (e.g. “soon”) without providing that information should score 0
for non-responsiveness. • A reasoned procedural objection about notice, timing, or fairness does not
by itself qualify as good deliberation. To receive a score of 1, the exchange must
also include substantive engagement with the objection, such as a direct answer,
justification, or concrete accommodation.

blocks.en: We constructed the corrected inductive codebook by merging the English and Hebrew codebooks, retaining every distinct metric from each. Where the two versions overlapped, we consolidated them into a single metric; Hebrew’s Decorum and Tone category was split between Procedural Decorum and Respectful Engagement. We removed most illustrative examples (“such as…”) to avoid biasing human or model annotators toward specific cases. We also adopted the bullet structure of the Hebrew codebook and standardized it so that every metric has two labeled poles, “High” and “Low”. Where a source codebook described only one pole, we defined the missing one to be the parallel opposite of the existing one. Finally, for the Procedural Decorum metric, we replaced “unanimous agreement” from the English codebook with “respectful disagreement”, since agreement is not a condition for good decorum.
blocks.zh: 我们通过合并英文和希伯来文的密码本,设计了经过校正的入门密码本,保留了每一本的分量。 在两个版本重叠的地方,我们将它们合并为一个标准;希伯来语的"装饰"和"通"分类被分为"程序装饰"和"尊重的约定". 我们删除了大多数说明性例子(“例如......”),以避免将人或模型说明员偏向于具体案件。 我们还采用了希伯来语编码手册的弹道结构,并将其标准化,使每一公尺都有“高”和“低”两个标记杆。 当一个源代码书只描述出一杆时,我们把缺失的一杆定义为与已存在的一杆相平行. 最后,就程序标准而言,我们用“尊重的不同意见”取代了英文法典中的“一致协议”,因为协议不是良好礼仪的条件。

blocks.en: 0. Demand A proposal about what should or should not be decided or done. A demand may support changing, adopting, rejecting, or preserving a policy or course of action. 1. Participation Definition: Evaluates whether a participant can complete a relevant contribution without being prevented from speaking by disruption or formal intervention. Coding Categories / Scale: Code 0 (Participation Interrupted): The speaker explicitly indicates that an interruption is disturbing or preventing the contribution, or the contribution is terminated by a formal decision. Do not assign this code merely because the allocated speaking time has expired. Code 1 (Normal Participation Possible): The participant is able to make the relevant contribution under ordinary speaking conditions. 2. Level of Justification for Demands Definition: Measures the completeness of the reasons supplied for a demand. The substantive truth or persuasiveness of the argument is not judged. A complete justification contains (1) a conclusion about what should or should not be done, (2) a supporting reason, and (3) an explicit or unmistakably implied inferential link between the reason and conclusion. Coding Categories / Scale: Code 0 (No Justification): A demand or evaluation is stated, but no supporting reason is provided. Code 1 (Inferior Justification): A supporting consideration is mentioned, but the link between the reason and the demand is incomplete or unclear. A conclusion supported only by illustration also receives Code 1. Code 2 (Qualified Justification): At least one complete justification connects a demand to a reason through an explicit or clearly implied inferential link. Code 3 (Sophisticated Justification): At least two distinct complete justifications are supplied, whether for the same demand or for different demands within the speech act. Decision Rule: Assign the highest level whose requirements are fully met. An implicit linkage counts only when its intended meaning would be beyond reasonable doubt to participants in the debate. 3. Content of Justification for Demands Definition: Identifies whose interests are explicitly invoked when a speaker justifies a demand: a constituency or particular group, society collectively, or disadvantaged groups under a fairness-based conception of the common good. Coding Categories: Code 0 (Constituency or Group Interest): At least one explicit appeal is made to the interest of a particular constituency, organization, sector, party, region, or social group. Code 1 (Neutral Statement): There is no explicit reference to a constituency or group interest and no explicit appeal to either form of the common good. Code 2 (Common-Good Orientation): The speaker explicitly justifies a demand using at least one of the following forms of common-good reasoning: Utilitarian or Collective Common Good: An appeal to the best outcome for the greatest number, society as a whole, or a larger collective such as Europe or humanity. Difference-Principle Common Good: An appeal to protecting or helping the least advantaged, poorest, most discriminated against, or otherwise vulnerable members of society, including children and future generations, or an appeal to fairness and justice in this sense. Decision Rule: Assign the highest level whose requirements are fully met. 4. Respect toward Groups to Be Helped (Empathy) Definition: Evaluates how the speaker characterizes the people or groups who would be affected or helped by the demand. Coding Categories / Scale: Code 0 (No Respect): At least one negative or degrading statement is made about a relevant group, and no positive statement is made. A single negative statement is sufficient. Code 1 (Neutral): Neither negative nor explicitly positive statements are made about the relevant groups. Code 2 (Explicit Respect): At least one explicitly positive, valuing, empathetic, or dignity-affirming statement is made about a relevant group. This code still applies when negative statements also occur. Priority Rule: Explicit respect takes priority over negativity: mixed positive and negative statements receive Code 2. 5. Respect toward the Demands of Others Definition: Evaluates whether a speaker degrades, treats neutrally, or explicitly values demands advanced by other participants. Coding Categories / Scale: Code 0 (No Respect): At least one negative or degrading statement is made toward another demand, or toward the person or group advancing it, and no positive statement is made. Code 1 (Neutral): Other demands receive neither negative nor explicitly positive treatment. Code 2 (Explicit Respect): At least one positive statement values any aspect of another participant’s demand. This code still applies when negative statements also occur. N/A (Not Applicable): Only one demand is on the agenda and the speaker supports it; consequently, there is no distinct competing demand to evaluate. Priority Rule: Explicit respect takes priority over negativity: mixed positive and negative statements receive Code 2. Criticism of another demand may additionally be coded under Level and Content of Justification when it functions as part of the speaker’s own argument. 6. Respect toward Counterarguments Definition: Evaluates how a speaker responds to arguments that contradict the speaker’s conclusion concerning a demand. The category concerns engagement with opposing reasons, not merely interpersonal politeness. Coding Categories / Scale: Code 0 (Counterarguments Ignored): One or more counterarguments are already available, but the speaker does not address any of them. Code 1 (Included but Explicitly Degraded): Counterarguments are acknowledged, but at least one is degraded, mocked, or attacked, and none is explicitly valued. Attacks on the people or groups advancing the counterarguments also count. Code 2 (Included Neutrally): Counterarguments are acknowledged or addressed without either negative degradation or explicit positive valuation. Code 3 (Included and Explicitly Valued): At least one aspect of at least one counterargument is explicitly recognized as valid, correct, useful, or worthy of consideration. This code still applies when other negative statements occur. N/A (Not Applicable): No counterargument has yet been introduced and the speaker does not anticipate one. Totality Rule: When several counterarguments exist, assign one code to the speaker’s treatment of the set as a whole. Explicit valuation takes priority over negative treatment; without valuation, any degradation leads to Code 1. An anticipated counterargument should receive an actual code rather than N/A. 7. Constructive Politics Definition: Measures whether the speaker remains fixed in a position or advances a mediating proposal, distinguishing proposals that address the present agenda from alternatives that belong to another policy agenda. Coding Categories / Scale: Code 0 (Positional Politics): The speaker maintains a position without offering a mediating or compromise proposal. Code 1 (Alternative Proposal): The speaker advances a proposal that could mediate the broader conflict but does not fit the current agenda or resolve the decision presently under debate. It would need to be considered under another agenda. Code 2 (Mediating Proposal): The speaker offers a concrete compromise or accommodation within the current agenda that attempts to bridge competing concerns or modify the proposal under consideration. Coding Note: A proposal is not mediating merely because it differs from the current proposal. It must attempt to accommodate competing concerns; the distinction between Codes 1 and 2 depends on whether it can be acted upon within the present agenda.

Code 1 (Neutral Statement): There is no explicit reference to a constituency or group interest and no explicit appeal to either form of the common good. Code 2 (Common-Good Orientation): The speaker explicitly justifies a demand using at least one of the following forms of common-good reasoning: Utilitarian or Collective Common Good: An appeal to the best outcome for the greatest number, society as a whole, or a larger collective such as Europe or humanity. Difference-Principle Common Good: An appeal to protecting or helping the least advantaged, poorest, most discriminated against, or otherwise vulnerable members of society, including children and future generations, or an appeal to fairness and justice in this sense. Decision Rule: Assign the highest level whose requirements are fully met.

blocks.en: 6. Respect toward Counterarguments Definition: Evaluates how a speaker responds to arguments that contradict the speaker’s conclusion concerning a demand. The category concerns engagement with opposing reasons, not merely interpersonal politeness. Coding Categories / Scale: Code 0 (Counterarguments Ignored): One or more counterarguments are already available, but the speaker does not address any of them. Code 1 (Included but Explicitly Degraded): Counterarguments are acknowledged, but at least one is degraded, mocked, or attacked, and none is explicitly valued. Attacks on the people or groups advancing the counterarguments also count. Code 2 (Included Neutrally): Counterarguments are acknowledged or addressed without either negative degradation or explicit positive valuation. Code 3 (Included and Explicitly Valued): At least one aspect of at least one counterargument is explicitly recognized as valid, correct, useful, or worthy of consideration. This code still applies when other negative statements occur. N/A (Not Applicable): No counterargument has yet been introduced and the speaker does not anticipate one. Totality Rule: When several counterarguments exist, assign one code to the speaker’s treatment of the set as a whole. Explicit valuation takes priority over negative treatment; without valuation, any degradation leads to Code 1. An anticipated counterargument should receive an actual code rather than N/A.

Constructive Politics Definition: Measures whether the speaker remains fixed in a position or advances a mediating proposal, distinguishing proposals that address the present agenda from alternatives that belong to another policy agenda. Coding Categories / Scale: Code 0 (Positional Politics): The speaker maintains a position without offering a mediating or compromise proposal. Code 1 (Alternative Proposal): The speaker advances a proposal that could mediate the broader conflict but does not fit the current agenda or resolve the decision presently under debate. It would need to be considered under another agenda. Code 2 (Mediating Proposal): The speaker offers a concrete compromise or accommodation within the current agenda that attempts to bridge competing concerns or modify the proposal under consideration. Coding Note: A proposal is not mediating merely because it differs from the current proposal. It must attempt to accommodate competing concerns; the distinction between Codes 1 and 2 depends on whether it can be acted upon within the present agenda.

blocks.en: Metric 1: Procedural Decorum This metric evaluates the extent to which participants follow parliamentary rules, wait for their turn to speak, and avoid shouting or talking over one another. In some committees, the chairperson must repeatedly threaten to remove members to maintain order. Conversely, other meetings proceed with unanimous agreement, polite praises, and uninterrupted presentations. Metric 2: Topic Adherence This metric measures the ratio of substantive discussion regarding the agenda versus unrelated political grandstanding or personal attacks. High topic adherence is observed when members strictly debate specific legal definitions, such as defining security offenses versus treason. Low adherence occurs when speaking time meant for legislative reservations is entirely used to attack political opponents on unrelated national issues. Metric 3: Constructive Problem-Solving This metric assesses the ability of committee members and government officials to bridge disagreements and reach practical legislative compromises. This metric is positive when members negotiate temporary orders to test a law’s impact before making it permanent. It is also evident when legal advisors and ministries successfully negotiate timelines for administrative tasks, such as extending a deadline from three months to seven months to accommodate workload constraints. Metric 4: Respectful Engagement This metric analyzes the tone and language used when interacting with civil servants, academic experts, and members of the public. Discourse quality drops when elected officials use dismissive language, such as calling opposing arguments “bullshit”. It also drops when there is friction between politicians and civil servants, such as when an official allegedly calls a member a “populist”. High quality is shown when chairpersons actively listen to and validate the emotional testimonies of local mayors. Metric 5: Emotional Regulation This metric examines how the committee handles highly charged emotional topics or national tragedies while conducting legislative business. Poor emotional regulation is visible when procedural duties, like budget discussions, clash with days of national mourning, leading to accusations of callousness and “disgusting” behavior between members. High emotional tension is also present when bereaved parents confront lawmakers directly during security-related debates.
blocks.zh: 计量1:程序装饰 这一衡量标准评估了参与者遵守议会规则的程度,等待他们发言,并避免相互大叫或交谈。 在一些委员会中,主席必须一再威胁要罢免成员以维持秩序。 相反,其他会议则以一致一致、礼貌地赞扬和不间断地发言的方式进行。 计量2:专题遵守 这一衡量尺度衡量关于议程的实质性讨论与无关的政治夸大或个人攻击的比例。 在成员严格辩论具体的法律定义,例如界定安全罪与叛国罪时,遵守高主题。 当立法保留的发言时间被完全用来攻击政治对手处理无关的国家问题时,就会出现加入率低的情况。 计量 3: 建设性问题解决 这一衡量标准评估了委员会成员和政府官员弥合分歧并达成实际立法妥协的能力。 当成员谈判临时命令以测试某项法律的影响然后使之永久化时,这一标准是积极的。 同样明显的是,法律顾问和各部成功地就行政任务时间表进行谈判,例如将最后期限从3个月延长到7个月,以应付工作量限制。 计量4:尊重参与 这一衡量标准分析了与公务员,学术专家和公众成员互动时所使用的语气和语言. 当当选官员使用辞退语言时,如将对立论点称为“胡说八道”。 当政治家和公务员之间发生摩擦时,例如,据称一名官员称某一成员为“民粹主义者”。 当主席们积极听取和验证地方市长的情感证词时,就显示出高质量的表现。 计量 5: 情绪调节 这一衡量标准审查了委员会如何在从事立法工作时处理高度紧张的情绪话题或国家悲剧。 当程序性职责,如预算讨论,与全国哀悼日相冲突,导致指责成员之间冷酷无情和“令人厌恶”的行为时,情绪管制就很明显。 当死者父母在与安全有关的辩论中直接面对立法者时,情绪也高度紧张。

Poor emotional regulation is visible when procedural duties, like budget discussions, clash with days of national mourning, leading to accusations of callousness and “disgusting” behavior between members. High emotional tension is also present when bereaved parents confront lawmakers directly during security-related debates.
blocks.zh: 计量 5: 情绪调节 这一衡量标准审查了委员会如何在从事立法工作时处理高度紧张的情绪话题或国家悲剧。 当程序性职责,如预算讨论,与全国哀悼日相冲突,导致指责成员之间冷酷无情和“令人厌恶”的行为时,情绪管制就很明显。 当死者父母在与安全有关的辩论中直接面对立法者时,情绪也高度紧张。

blocks.en: Metric 1: Procedural Decorum Evaluates the extent to which participants follow parliamentary rules, wait for their turn to speak, and avoid shouting or talking over one another. High Decorum: Observed in meetings that proceed with polite exchanges, uninterrupted presentations, and respectful disagreement. Low Decorum: Associated with committees where the chairperson must repeatedly threaten to remove members to maintain order. Metric 2: Topic Adherence Measures the ratio of substantive discussion regarding the agenda versus unrelated political grandstanding or personal attacks. High Adherence: Observed when the majority of participants strictly stick to the discussion agenda, debating specific outcomes and legal definitions. Low Adherence: Observed when discussions frequently go off-topic, or when speaking time meant for legislative reservations is entirely used to attack political opponents on unrelated national issues. Metric 3: Constructive Problem-Solving Assesses the ability of committee members and government officials to bridge disagreements and reach practical legislative compromises. High Constructiveness: Indicated by members negotiating temporary orders to test a law’s impact before making it permanent, or when legal advisors and ministries successfully negotiate timelines for administrative tasks. Low Constructiveness: Indicated by members adopting zero-sum ideological positions that lead to legislative deadlocks, or government ministries engaging in jurisdictional turf wars and blame-shifting instead of finding actionable paths forward. Metric 4: Respectful Engagement Analyzes the tone and language used when interacting with civil servants, academic experts, and members of the public. High Respect: Demonstrated when participants utilize active listening, validate each other’s opinions, and maintain a professional tone. Low Respect: Characterized by friction between participants and the use of dismissive or vulgar language (e.g., calling opposing arguments “bullshit”). Metric 5: Emotional Regulation Examines how the committee handles highly charged emotional topics or national tragedies while conducting legislative business. High Regulation: Demonstrated when lawmakers maintain composure, empathy, and respect during emotionally charged testimonies. The committee successfully balances sensitivity to national tragedies with its legislative duties without allowing the discussion to devolve into chaos. Low Regulation: Demonstrated when routine business clashes with sensitive events, resulting in insults, accusations of callousness, or uncontrolled tension when lawmakers are confronted by grieving citizens. Metric 6: Meeting Management Effectiveness Examines the committee chairperson’s ability to control the discussion, steer it toward practical decisions, cut off disruptions, and prevent the debate from spiraling out of control, all while maintaining fairness. High Effectiveness: The chairperson successfully cuts short lengthy bureaucratic arguments, guides professional entities to reach practical compromises, makes on-the-spot decisions, and holds parties accountable for failing to perform their duties. Low Effectiveness: Characterized by a loss of control over the speaking order, repeated attempts to quiet heckling, and frequent but unsuccessful threats to remove participants from the room. Metric 7: Professionalism and Reliance on Data Assesses the extent to which committee participants rely on facts, data, and research, and their attentiveness to professional echelons and legal counsel. High Professionalism: Characterized by a meticulous, section-by-section analysis of the law alongside legal counsel, demonstrating an understanding of the legal implications of the legislation. Compromises set realistic timetables in coordination with professional authorities. Low Professionalism: Characterized by participants ignoring research and data, disregarding professional or legal advice, and arguing over legislation without understanding its technical or practical implications.

Low Decorum: Associated with committees where the chairperson must repeatedly threaten to remove members to maintain order.

blocks.en: 1. Level of Justification (Argumentative Rationality) Theoretical Origin: Discourse Quality Index (Steenbergen et al., 2003); Stromer-Galley (2007); Friess & Eilders (2015). Definition: Evaluates the logical structure and completeness of reasons provided by Members of the Knesset (MKs) or invited witnesses when advancing a policy proposal, amendment, or claim. Coding Categories / Scale: Level 0 (No Justification): A demand/claim is stated without any supporting reason. Level 1 (Inferior Justification): A reason is stated, but the logical link between the demand and the reason is incomplete or relies strictly on illustration. Level 2 (Qualified Justification): At least one complete, explicit, or clearly implied inferential link connects the demand to a supporting reason. Level 3 (Sophisticated Justification): At least two distinct, complete inferential links are provided (either multiple complete reasons for one demand or reasons spanning multiple demands). 2. Content of Justification (Common Good Orientation) Theoretical Origin: Steenbergen et al. (2003); Habermas (1996); Cohen (1989). Definition: Assesses whether a speaker justifies claims solely through narrow sectoral/party/constituency interests or frames arguments in terms of broader societal benefit. Coding Categories / Scale: Group/Constituency Interest: Explicit appeals to narrow political, regional, or constituency benefits. Neutral Statement: No explicit reference to either narrow group interests or the broader common good. Common Good (Utilitarian): Explicit appeal to the best outcome for Israeli society as a whole or the greatest benefit for the majority. Common Good (Difference Principle): Explicit appeal to protecting or helping the least advantaged, vulnerable, or marginalized groups in society (Rawlsian difference principle). 3. Sourcing and Evidence Base Theoretical Origin: Stromer-Galley (2007); Friess & Eilders (2015). Definition: Measures the extent to which participants support their positions using verifiable external references, expert testimonies, or official materials rather than unsupported assertions. Coding Categories: Official/Committee Documents: Reference to Knesset Research and Information Center (MMM) reports, ministry briefings, or draft bill texts. External/Expert Sources: Reference to academic research, statistical data, court rulings, or international benchmarks. Mass Media: Reference to news reports, journalism, or public media broadcasts. Personal Experience / Narrative: Reference to first-hand accounts, constituent stories, or personal anecdotes. No Source: Claim made without grounding in external or experiential sources. 4. Interactivity and Reciprocity Theoretical Origin: Stromer-Galley (2007); Friess & Eilders (2015). Definition: Evaluates whether committee dialogue constitutes a genuine, reciprocal exchange of ideas where speakers listen and respond to one another, or consists of disconnected monologues (“soap-boxing”). Coding Indicators: Formal Interactivity: Whether a speech turn explicitly addresses a prior speaker or turn. Substantive Interactivity: Whether a speaker directly addresses, rebuts, clarifies, or builds upon the specific arguments made by a prior participant. Information-Seeking / Questioning: Presence of genuine questions aimed at eliciting clarification or facts from witnesses, government officials, or fellow MKs (distinguished from rhetorical questions). Clarification (Self/Other): Speech acts that explicitly clarify a speaker’s own prior position or summarize another participant’s argument to verify understanding. 5. Respect and Civility toward Actors and Demands Theoretical Origin: Steenbergen et al. (2003); Young (1996); Friess & Eilders (2015). Definition: Measures the interpersonal tone and level of mutual recognition accorded to other participants, social groups, and policy proposals during committee proceedings. Coding Categories / Scale: Respect toward Groups: Evaluates whether social, ethnic, or political groups affected by the bill are degraded (0), treated neutrally (1), or explicitly valued/respected (2). Respect toward Demands: Evaluates whether policy proposals/amendments raised by fellow participants are degraded/insulted (0), treated neutrally (1), explicitly valued (2), or agreed with (3). Civility / Disruption: Tracks presence of personal insults, ad hominem attacks, or unprocedural interruptions. 6. Engagement with Counterarguments Theoretical Origin: Steenbergen et al. (2003); Bächtiger et al. (2010). Definition: Assesses how speakers handle opposing viewpoints or counterarguments raised by coalition/opposition members or invited experts. Coding Categories / Scale: Level 0 (Ignored): Counterarguments exist on the table, but the speaker completely ignores them. Level 1 (Included but Degraded): Counterarguments are acknowledged but explicitly degraded, mocked, or dismissed without substantive engagement. Level 2 (Included Neutrally): Counterarguments are acknowledged and restated neutrally without personal or thematic degradation. Level 3 (Included and Valued): Counterarguments are acknowledged and explicitly praised or treated as valid considerations, even if ultimately rejected or integrated. 7. Constructive Politics and Compromise Orientation Theoretical Origin: Steenbergen et al. (2003); Bächtiger et al. (2010); Friess & Eilders (2015). Definition: Measures whether committee participants remain locked in rigid, zero-sum partisan stances or actively attempt to build consensus and formulate acceptable compromises. Coding Categories / Scale: Positional Politics (Level 0): Speakers rigidly maintain initial party lines without attempt at compromise, accommodation, or reconciliation. Alternative Proposal (Level 1): A mediating proposal is offered that belongs to a different agenda or jurisdiction, failing to resolve the immediate conflict on the current draft text. Mediating Proposal (Level 2): A speaker advances a concrete, integrative compromise or amendment that directly fits the current agenda and seeks to bridge coalition-opposition or stakeholder divides. 8. Topic Coherence and Agenda Focus Theoretical Origin: Stromer-Galley (2007); Friess & Eilders (2015). Definition: Evaluates whether committee discussion stays focused on the legislative agenda (structuring topic) or drifts into uncoordinated, off-topic partisan disputes (interactional topic drift). Coding Indicators: On-Topic (Structuring): Statements directly addressing the bill, policy options, or specific committee agenda items. On-Topic (Related Problem): Statements addressing the broader policy issue (e.g., educational quality, defense budget) without directly addressing the specific legislative choices at hand. Off-Topic / Drift: Statements digressing into unrelated political scandals, electoral grandstanding, or personal disputes unlinked to the agenda. 9. Participatory Equality and Vocal Distribution Theoretical Origin: Stromer-Galley (2007); Knight & Johnson (1997); Friess & Eilders (2015). Definition: Measures whether speaking opportunities and floor time are equitably distributed among participants or monopolized by committee chairs, coalition members, or dominant speakers. Coding Indicators: Turn & Word-Count Distribution: Quantitative balance of speech turns and word volume across coalition vs. opposition MKs, and committee members vs. invited external experts/citizens. Procedural Equal Access: Absence of arbitrary silencing, unequal time enforcement by the chair, or procedural coercion that prevents backbenchers or opposition members from presenting amendments. 10. Inclusion of Alternative Communicative Modes Theoretical Origin: Young (1996); Bächtiger et al. (2010) (Type II Deliberation). Definition: Captures non-canonical speech forms—such as narrative/storytelling, rhetoric, and formal greeting—that complement formal argumentation by bridging cultural, ideological, or experiential divides in parliamentary committees. Coding Categories: Narrative / Testimony: Use of situated personal stories, constituent accounts, or lived experiences to demonstrate legislative impact or illuminate marginalized perspectives. Rhetoric / Expressive Language: Use of emotional resonance, figurative language, or metaphor to contextualize policy claims and engage listeners. Greeting and Deference: Use of formal politeness, honorifics, or conciliatory gestures that acknowledge the standing of opponents and establish deliberative trust.
blocks.zh: 1. 联合国 合理性(参数性)理论起源:论文质量指数(Steenbergen等,2003年);Stromer-Galley(2007年);Friess & Eilders(2015年)。 定义: 评估议会成员或被邀请的证人在提出政策建议、修正或主张时提供的理由的逻辑结构和完整性。 编码类别/ 尺度: 0级( 无正当理由) : 要求/索赔是在没有任何支持理由的情况下提出的。 第1级(粗略说明): 陈述了一个理由,但需求与理由之间的逻辑联系是不完整的或严格依赖插图. 第二级(合格理由): 至少有一个完整、明确或明显暗示的暗示联系将需求与支持性理由联系起来。 第三级(简单说明): 至少提供了两个截然不同的、完整的推断联系(要么是出于一个要求的多个完整理由,要么是因为跨越多个要求的原因)。 2. 合理性(共同良好取向)理论起源:Steenbergen等人(2003年);Habermas(1996年);Cohen(1989年)。 定义: 评估发言者是否仅仅通过狭隘的部门/党派/选区利益来证明索赔的合理性,或从更广泛的社会利益的角度来提出论据。 编码类别/规模:组/组 利益:明确呼吁减少政治、区域或选区利益。 中立声明 : 没有明确提及狭隘的集团利益或更广泛的共同利益。 共同好(Utilarian):明确呼吁以色列整个社会取得最佳结果,或为大多数人带来最大利益。 共同利益(差异原则): 明确呼吁保护或帮助社会中处境最不利的弱势群体或边缘化群体(罗尔西亚差异原则)。 3. 证据和证据基础理论起源:Stromer-Galley(2007);Friess & Eilders (2015年)。 定义: 衡量参与者使用可核查的外部参考、专家证词或官方材料而不是无根据的断言来支持其立场的程度。 编码类别:官员/委员会 文件:参考以色列议会研究和信息中心的报告、部委简报或法案文本草案。 外部/专家来源: 参考学术研究、统计数据、法院裁决或国际基准。 大众媒体: 参考新闻报道、新闻或公共媒体广播。 个人经验/叙述: 参考第一手资料 组成故事 或个人传闻 资料来源:在没有外部或经验来源依据的情况下提出的索赔。 4. 互动和对等理论起源:Stromer-Galley(2007年);Friess & Eilders (2015年)。 定义: 评估委员会对话是否构成真正的、对等的意见交流,使发言者相互倾听并作出反应,还是由相互脱节的独白(“肥皂盒”)。 编码指标:正式互动: 发言是明确针对前面的发言者,还是转向。 实质性互动: 发言者是否直接针对、反驳、澄清或依据前与会者提出的具体论点。 信息查询/问: 存在真正问题,旨在从证人、政府官员或MK伙伴那里获得澄清或事实(有别于口头问题)。 澄清(自行/其他): 发言行为明确澄清发言者自己的立场或总结另一与会者的论点以核实理解。 5. 对行为者和要求理论渊源的尊重和文明:Steenbergen等人(2003年);Young(1996年);Friess & Eilders(2015年)。 定义: 衡量委员会会议期间给予其他参与者、社会群体和政策建议的人际关系和相互承认的程度。 编码类别/规模:尊重群体: 评估受该法案影响的社会、族裔或政治团体是否退化(0个)、是否受到中立对待(1个)、或是否受到明确重视/尊重(2个)。 尊重要求: 评估其他参与者提出的政策建议/修正是退化/被侮辱(0)、受到中立对待(1)、受到明确重视(2个),还是与(3)商定。 文明/混乱: 追踪个人侮辱、人身攻击或非程序性干扰。 6. 与辩证理论渊源的接触:Steenbergen等人(2003年);Bächtiger等人(2010年)。 定义: 评估发言者如何处理联盟/反对派成员或应邀专家提出的反对意见或反驳意见。 编码类别/规模:0级(被忽略): 桌上存在反驳,但演讲者完全无视. 1级(包含但已降解): 在没有实质性参与的情况下,辩驳被承认,但被明确贬低、嘲弄或驳回。 第二级( 中性 ) : 辩驳意见在没有个人或专题退化的情况下得到确认和中立地重申。 第三级(包含和价值): 反驳被承认并被明确称赞或视为有效的考虑,即使最终被拒绝或并入。 7. 建设性政治和妥协取向理论渊源:Steenbergen等人(2003年);Bächtiger等人(2010年);Friess & Eilders(2015年)。 定义:衡量委员会成员是否仍然被僵硬、零和的党派立场所束缚,或是否积极试图建立共识并拟订可接受的妥协。 编码类别/ 尺度: 位置政治( 0级) : 发言者严格维持最初的政党路线,而不试图妥协、妥协或和解。 备选提案(一级): 提出的调解提案属于不同的议程或法域,未能解决当前案文草案的直接冲突。 调解建议(二级): 发言者提出具体、综合的妥协或修正案,直接符合目前的议程并力求弥合联盟-反对派或利益攸关方的分歧。 8. 专题一致性和议程重点理论渊源:Stromer-Galley(2007年);Friess & Eilders(2015年)。 定义: 评估委员会讨论的重点是否仍然是立法议程(安排专题),还是转向未经协调的、非专题的党派争端(互动专题漂移)。 编码指标:在线(结构): Eilders(2015年)。 定义:衡量发言机会和会场时间是否在与会者之间公平分配,或者由委员会主席、联盟成员或主要发言者垄断。 编码指标: 转接( W) -- -- 数据分布 : 跨联盟与反对派MK, 委员会成员与应邀的外聘专家/公民的言论和字数平衡。 程序上的平等机会:主席没有任意的沉默、不平等的时间执行,或程序上的胁迫,使背信弃义者或反对派成员无法提出修正案。 10. 列入替代交流模式理论起源:Young(1996年);Bächtiger等人(2010年)(第二期审议)。 定义:抓住非讽刺性言论形式——如叙事/叙事、口才和正式问候——通过弥合议会委员会的文化、意识形态或经验分歧来补充正式论点。 编码类别 : 叙述/证词: 利用定位的个人故事、组成说法或活生生的经验来展示立法影响或阐明边缘化观点。 热力/ 表达式语言: 使用情感共鸣,比喻语言,或比喻来将政策主张的背景化并吸引听众参与. 问候与尊重:使用正式的礼貌,荣誉,或和解姿态,承认对手的地位并建立起议事信任.

blocks.en: 1. Level of Justification (Argumentative Rationality) Theoretical Origin: Discourse Quality Index (Steenbergen et al., 2003); Stromer-Galley (2007); Friess & Eilders (2015). Definition: Evaluates the logical structure and completeness of reasons provided by Members of the Knesset (MKs) or invited witnesses when advancing a policy proposal, amendment, or claim. Coding Categories / Scale: Level 0 (No Justification): A demand/claim is stated without any supporting reason. Level 1 (Inferior Justification): A reason is stated, but the logical link between the demand and the reason is incomplete or relies strictly on illustration. Level 2 (Qualified Justification): At least one complete, explicit, or clearly implied inferential link connects the demand to a supporting reason. Level 3 (Sophisticated Justification): At least two distinct, complete inferential links are provided (either multiple complete reasons for one demand or reasons spanning multiple demands).

blocks.en: 2. Content of Justification (Common Good Orientation) Theoretical Origin: Steenbergen et al. (2003); Habermas (1996); Cohen (1989). Definition: Assesses whether a speaker justifies claims solely through narrow sectoral/party/constituency interests or frames arguments in terms of broader societal benefit. Coding Categories / Scale: Group/Constituency Interest: Explicit appeals to narrow political, regional, or constituency benefits. Neutral Statement: No explicit reference to either narrow group interests or the broader common good. Common Good (Utilitarian): Explicit appeal to the best outcome for Israeli society as a whole or the greatest benefit for the majority. Common Good (Difference Principle): Explicit appeal to protecting or helping the least advantaged, vulnerable, or marginalized groups in society (Rawlsian difference principle).

blocks.en: 4. Interactivity and Reciprocity Theoretical Origin: Stromer-Galley (2007); Friess & Eilders (2015). Definition: Evaluates whether committee dialogue constitutes a genuine, reciprocal exchange of ideas where speakers listen and respond to one another, or consists of disconnected monologues (“soap-boxing”). Coding Indicators: Formal Interactivity: Whether a speech turn explicitly addresses a prior speaker or turn. Substantive Interactivity: Whether a speaker directly addresses, rebuts, clarifies, or builds upon the specific arguments made by a prior participant. Information-Seeking / Questioning: Presence of genuine questions aimed at eliciting clarification or facts from witnesses, government officials, or fellow MKs (distinguished from rhetorical questions). Clarification (Self/Other): Speech acts that explicitly clarify a speaker’s own prior position or summarize another participant’s argument to verify understanding.

blocks.en: 5. Respect and Civility toward Actors and Demands Theoretical Origin: Steenbergen et al. (2003); Young (1996); Friess & Eilders (2015). Definition: Measures the interpersonal tone and level of mutual recognition accorded to other participants, social groups, and policy proposals during committee proceedings. Coding Categories / Scale: Respect toward Groups: Evaluates whether social, ethnic, or political groups affected by the bill are degraded (0), treated neutrally (1), or explicitly valued/respected (2). Respect toward Demands: Evaluates whether policy proposals/amendments raised by fellow participants are degraded/insulted (0), treated neutrally (1), explicitly valued (2), or agreed with (3). Civility / Disruption: Tracks presence of personal insults, ad hominem attacks, or unprocedural interruptions.

blocks.en: 6. Engagement with Counterarguments Theoretical Origin: Steenbergen et al. (2003); Bächtiger et al. (2010). Definition: Assesses how speakers handle opposing viewpoints or counterarguments raised by coalition/opposition members or invited experts. Coding Categories / Scale: Level 0 (Ignored): Counterarguments exist on the table, but the speaker completely ignores them. Level 1 (Included but Degraded): Counterarguments are acknowledged but explicitly degraded, mocked, or dismissed without substantive engagement. Level 2 (Included Neutrally): Counterarguments are acknowledged and restated neutrally without personal or thematic degradation. Level 3 (Included and Valued): Counterarguments are acknowledged and explicitly praised or treated as valid considerations, even if ultimately rejected or integrated.

blocks.en: 7. Constructive Politics and Compromise Orientation Theoretical Origin: Steenbergen et al. (2003); Bächtiger et al. (2010); Friess & Eilders (2015). Definition: Measures whether committee participants remain locked in rigid, zero-sum partisan stances or actively attempt to build consensus and formulate acceptable compromises. Coding Categories / Scale: Positional Politics (Level 0): Speakers rigidly maintain initial party lines without attempt at compromise, accommodation, or reconciliation. Alternative Proposal (Level 1): A mediating proposal is offered that belongs to a different agenda or jurisdiction, failing to resolve the immediate conflict on the current draft text. Mediating Proposal (Level 2): A speaker advances a concrete, integrative compromise or amendment that directly fits the current agenda and seeks to bridge coalition-opposition or stakeholder divides.
blocks.zh: 7. 联合国 建设性政治和妥协取向理论起源:Steenbergen等人(2003年);Bächtiger等人(2010年);Friess & Eilders(2015年)。 定义:衡量委员会成员是否仍然被僵硬、零和的党派立场所束缚,或是否积极试图建立共识并拟订可接受的妥协。 编码类别/ 尺度: 位置政治( 0级) : 发言者严格维持最初的政党路线,而不试图妥协、妥协或和解。 备选提案(一级): 提出的调解提案属于不同的议程或法域,未能解决当前案文草案的直接冲突。 调解建议(二级): 发言者提出具体、综合的妥协或修正案,直接符合目前的议程并力求弥合联盟-反对派或利益攸关方的分歧。

blocks.zh: 职位政治( 0级): 发言者严格维持最初的政党路线,而不试图妥协、妥协或和解。

blocks.en: 8. Topic Coherence and Agenda Focus Theoretical Origin: Stromer-Galley (2007); Friess & Eilders (2015). Definition: Evaluates whether committee discussion stays focused on the legislative agenda (structuring topic) or drifts into uncoordinated, off-topic partisan disputes (interactional topic drift). Coding Indicators: On-Topic (Structuring): Statements directly addressing the bill, policy options, or specific committee agenda items. On-Topic (Related Problem): Statements addressing the broader policy issue (e.g., educational quality, defense budget) without directly addressing the specific legislative choices at hand. Off-Topic / Drift: Statements digressing into unrelated political scandals, electoral grandstanding, or personal disputes unlinked to the agenda.
blocks.zh: 8. 联合国 主题一致性和议程焦点理论起源:Stromer-Galley(2007年);Friess & Eilders (2015年)。 定义: 评估委员会讨论的重点是否仍然是立法议程(安排专题),还是转向未经协调的、非专题的党派争端(互动专题漂移)。 编码指标:在线(结构): 直接就法案、政策选择或具体委员会议程项目发言。 在线(有关问题): 发言涉及更广泛的政策问题(如教育质量、国防预算),但没有直接涉及手头的具体立法选择。 Off-Topic / Drift: 言论分裂为无关的政治丑闻,选举大权或个人纠纷与议程无关.
